issues.description: The script uses XMLHttpRequest to fetch external code and executes it via a[a][a](x.responseText), which is equivalent to eval(). This allows remote code execution from arbitrary URLs.
issues.recommendation: Remove dynamic code loading and execution. Only load trusted, versioned libraries via @require.

issues.description: The script stores and retrieves a UUID and a usage count in GM storage, which could be used for tracking users across sessions.
issues.recommendation: Do not store persistent identifiers unless strictly necessary. Document the purpose and limit scope.

issues.description: The script connects to ksw2-moomoo.glitch.me and uses GM_getTab/GM_saveTab to store tab objects, potentially transmitting user session data to a third-party server.
issues.recommendation: Avoid sending user data to third-party servers. Use local storage only.

issues.description: The script uses a[a][a](...) pattern, which is a form of obfuscation and indirect eval.
issues.recommendation: Avoid obfuscation and indirect code execution. Use clear, auditable code.

issues.description: The script uses innerHTML and document.getElementById, and may insert untrusted content without sanitization.
issues.recommendation: Sanitize all user input before inserting into the DOM.

issues.description: The script requests high privileges (unsafeWindow, GM_getTabs, GM_saveTab) but does not use all of them in the visible code.
issues.recommendation: Reduce privilege scope to only what is necessary.

issues.description: The script loads third-party libraries from greasyfork.org and code.jquery.com, but does not fix versions for msgpack.js and scijs.js (greasyfork URLs are mutable).
issues.recommendation: Pin all dependencies to versioned URLs or hashes.

issues.description: The script may create or manipulate iframes for recaptcha bypass and other purposes, which could be used for clickjacking or data extraction.
issues.recommendation: Avoid manipulating iframes unless necessary. Document all iframe usage.

summary: This userscript presents critical security risks, including remote code execution via dynamic loading and eval, persistent user tracking, third-party data transmission, code obfuscation, DOM XSS risk, excessive permissions, and supply chain vulnerabilities. It is not safe for use in its current form.
